title: Provide highly effective non-hormonal female contraception without an IUD

concept.text: Provide reversible, self-administered contraception with high pregnancy-prevention efficacy without hormones or an intrauterine procedure. Ovaprene is in phase 3, but its interim pregnancy observations do not establish this higher-efficacy target. Proposed completion test: FDA approval supported by a pivotal typical-use study covering at least 500 woman-years, with a Pearl Index below 2, adequate 13-cycle follow-up, acceptable local safety and prompt return to fertility. Test set by: Proposed editorial efficacy and exposure thresholds; FDA would decide approval. They are not the published Ovaprene performance goal. Sources given: [NICHD female contraceptive development programme](https://annualreport.nichd.nih.gov/blithe.html) ; [Daré regulatory and phase 3 disclosures](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1401914/000140191426000043/dare-20260630.htm) ; [Ovaprene interim trial observations](https://ir.darebioscience.com/news-releases/news-release-details/positive-interim-phase-3-results-highlight-potential-ovaprener-0).

page.title: Self-administered nonhormonal contraception with first-year typical-use pregnancy risk below 1%
page.definition: A reversible, hormone-free contraceptive that a woman administers herself without placing a device in the uterus. Fewer than 1% of users experience an unintended pregnancy during the first year of typical use, which includes inconsistent or incorrect use. Vaginal products are within scope. An existing nonhormonal vaginal gel, Phexxi, had a cumulative pregnancy probability of 13.7% over seven cycles in its pivotal trial.

goal.need: In surveys across 52 countries in 2005–2014, 26% of married women who wanted to avoid pregnancy and used no contraception cited side effects or health risks. In one year, about 17 in 100 diaphragm users and 21 in 100 internal-condom users become pregnant. A copper IUD offers greater protection but requires a clinician to place it in the uterus. Comparable protection from a method women use themselves would give those who wish to avoid both hormones and insertion another choice. Tolerability still matters: even a hormone-free vaginal gel can cause burning or itching.

completion.title: FDA authorizes a self-administered nonhormonal contraceptive with first-year typical-use failure below 1%.
completion.criterion: FDA grants marketing authorization for a reversible, self-administered, nonhormonal female contraceptive requiring no intrauterine placement. The accepted clinical evidence establishes fewer than 1 unintended pregnancy per 100 users during the first year of typical use, including incorrect or inconsistent use. Safety and reversibility are supported in the approved evidence package.
completion.set_by: Atlas fallback combining NICHD's FDA-approval objective with the HHS Tier 1 contraceptive-effectiveness category.
completion.basis: Searched FDA approval guidance, NICHD development programmes and HHS effectiveness classifications for a combined test covering efficacy, reversibility, self-administration and no hormones or IUD; none was found. This fallback joins NICHD's FDA-approval objective to HHS's Tier 1 typical-use category.

milestones.title: A contraceptive's laboratory and animal evidence supports initial human testing.
milestones.criterion: For a drug, preclinical pharmacology and toxicology data support a finding that initial human testing is reasonably safe. For a device requiring an investigational device exemption application, the report of prior investigations covers all prior clinical, animal and laboratory testing and provides adequate justification for the proposed human investigation.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Drug Development and Review Definitions for drugs and 21 CFR 812.27(a) for device investigations requiring an exemption application.
milestones.threshold_quote: Preclinical data to permit an assessment as to whether the product is reasonably safe for initial testing in humans.

milestones.title: A vaginal contraceptive reduces the mean count below 5 forward-moving sperm per high-power field.
milestones.criterion: For a vaginal product intended to impede sperm passage, examine midcycle cervical mucus two to four hours after intercourse. Average the number of progressively motile sperm across nine high-power microscope fields. A qualifying baseline cycle without the product averages at least 5 per field. A successful test cycle with the product averages fewer than 5 per field.
milestones.set_by: Ovaprene study investigators, registered study NCT03598088 and its published protocol methods. This test concerns vaginal contraceptives.
milestones.threshold_quote: A test cycle indicative of preliminary contraceptive effectiveness averaged < 5 progressively motile sperm/HPF.

milestones.title: A pivotal study of pregnancy prevention meets the requirements to begin enrollment.
milestones.criterion: The study may enroll participants at risk of pregnancy under the applicable regulatory pathway. A significant-risk device study requires FDA approval of the investigational device exemption and institutional review board approval. For a new study protocol under an investigational new drug application already in effect, the sponsor submits the protocol to FDA, obtains institutional review board approval and may proceed in the absence of a clinical hold.
milestones.set_by: FDA, IDE Approval Process for significant-risk devices and 21 CFR 312.30(a) for new protocols under an effective investigational new drug application.
milestones.threshold_quote: Studies of devices that pose a significant risk require both FDA and an Institutional Review Board (IRB) approval prior to initiation of a clinical study.

milestones.title: A pivotal study estimates first-year unintended pregnancy risk below 1% with typical use.
milestones.criterion: A completed pivotal study estimates the cumulative probability of unintended pregnancy during the first year of typical use at below 1%. The estimate covers incorrect or inconsistent use. A Pearl Index reports pregnancies per 100 woman-years of exposure and by itself does not provide the required first-year cumulative probability.
milestones.set_by: HHS Office of Population Affairs, Family Planning Annual Report: 2018 National Summary, Appendix C, page C-5. Tier 1 is an effectiveness classification, not Ovaprene's protocol performance goal.
milestones.threshold_quote: less than 1% of women experiencing an unintended pregnancy during the first year of typical use.

milestones.title: A contraceptive candidate shows activity through its proposed mechanism in a screening model.
milestones.criterion: In an in vitro or in vivo screening model, the candidate interferes with the reproductive process it targets, and the experiment confirms its mode of action. For a candidate intended to block fertilization, the model must show that effect as well as engagement of the proposed target.
milestones.set_by: Institute of Medicine, Committee on New Frontiers in Contraceptive Research, screening stage for lead compounds.
milestones.threshold_quote: effective in a screening model in which a mode of action can be confirmed in vitro or in vivo

not_found: No outside body was found defining the combined completion test for this capability.
No numerical Ovaprene Pearl Index performance goal was found in the opened developer disclosures.
The original FDA letters granting Ovaprene's IDE and approving its 2026 protocol amendment were not located.
ClinicalTrials.gov's accessible pages did not expose the full Ovaprene study records, and its study API could not be opened.
No common early pharmacodynamic threshold covering vaginal and systemic nonhormonal methods was found; the postcoital milestone applies to vaginal products.
The opened Ovaprene nonclinical disclosure did not provide the sheep study's sample size or detailed toxicology results.

results.finding: Intravaginal HC4-N reduced progressively motile human sperm by 100% versus PBS at the higher dose in a sheep model (n = 3 per antibody dose).
results.detail: The sheep model tested the antibody in solution and measured sperm motility in vaginal fluid two minutes after semen instillation.
results.quote:
Expressed as a percentage reduction in 
progressively motile sperm from that observed in the PBS control, the reduction was 
100% after instillation of 333 ug/mL (333 ug total dose), and 44% after instillation of 
33 ug/mL (33 ug total dose).

results.finding: Intravaginal ZB-06 had a no-observed-adverse-effect level of 5 mg/day in adult female rats (sample size unstated).
results.detail: The rat study included a 14-day recovery period. Minimal, reversible hematology changes at the high dose were judged nonadverse. The source is the sponsor’s protocol.
results.quote:
Based on the absence of any irritation or any toxicologically significant adverse effects in any 
of the parameters evaluated following daily intravaginal administration of ZB-06 for 9 days to 
adult female rats, the NOAEL for ZB-06 was considered to be 5 mg/day.

results.finding: Ovaprene averaged 0.5 progressively motile sperm per high-power field in both test cycles (38 enrolled, 23 completed).
results.detail: The nine-field averaging requirement cannot be verified from the supplied text.
results.quote: The mean of 27.2 (±17.9) progressively motile sperm/HPF in baseline postcoital test cycles was reduced to 0.5 (±1.1) and 0.5 (±1.3) progressively motile sperm/HPF in the first and second Ovaprene cycles, respectively.

results.finding: After ZB-06 use, vaginal swab eluates from all 8 participants agglutinated sperm in vitro.
results.quote: All eight vaginal swab eluates and 6/8 CM samples from Visit 7 (post ZB-06 use) were positive for sperm agglutination (p=0.0003 and p=0.002, respectively, Cochran’s Q test) whereas none of the vaginal swab and CM samples from the other (no product) visits exhibited sperm agglutination.

results.finding: After ZB-06 use, the 8 completers averaged 0.04 progressively motile sperm per high-power field.
results.quote: After use of a single ZB-06 film prior to intercourse, this number dropped to 0.04 (± 0.06) PMS/hpf (p<0.0001).

results.finding: The Phase III vaginal gel trial randomized 1,565 women at risk of pregnancy after institutional review board approval.
results.quote: The protocol was initiated after obtaining approval from the institutional review board of each center, the data-coordinating center, and the NIH.

results.finding: C31G vaginal gel (932 randomized) had a 13.8% first-year cumulative pregnancy probability in the modified intent-to-treat analysis.
results.detail: The primary endpoint was at six months. The optional extension had fewer participants, which reduced the precision of the 12-month estimates.
results.quote: Twelve-month pregnancy probabilities were 13.8% (95%CI 7.6–20%) for C31G and 19.8% (95%CI 10.9–28.7%) for nonoxynol-9.

results.finding: AMPOWER’s phase 3 Phexxi protocol received Advarra IRB approval and enrolled 1,384 women at risk of pregnancy.
results.detail: FDA consultation and agreement on study design are documented. The submission described in the methods was the statistical analysis plan before database lock.
results.quote: The study was conducted at 112 sites in the United States; the protocol was approved by The Advarra Institutional Review Board.

results.finding: Phexxi’s phase 3 AMPOWER analysis of 1,114 women estimated a seven-cycle typical-use cumulative pregnancy probability of 13.7%.
results.detail: The primary analysis limited qualifying cycles to 21–35 days with recorded vaginal intercourse and no backup or emergency contraception. It did not require correct and consistent gel use.
results.quote: a seven-cycle cumulative pregnancy percentage of 13.7% (95% CI: 10.0%–17.5%) with typical use

results.finding: Phexxi lowered pH and reduced sperm motility in vitro. Sample size and effect size were unreported.
results.detail: The FDA-approved label summarizes the mechanism studies in section 12.1 without describing a fertilization assay.
results.quote:
In vitro studies showed that a pH lowering effect and sperm motility reduction contribute to the activity 
of PHEXXI in the vagina.

results.finding: Phexxi (n=1183) had a 13.7% cumulative pregnancy probability over seven cycles of typical use.
results.detail: The analysis excluded cycles with backup contraception, cycles shorter than 21 or longer than 35 days, and cycles with no reported intercourse.
results.quote:
The 7-cycle cumulative pregnancy rate was 13.7% (95% 
CI: 10.0%, 17.5%), excluding cycles with back-up contraception, cycles <21 days or >35 days in 
length and cycles in which no intercourse was reported.

results.finding: Oral Org 9935 yielded 0 fertilized ova per rat in superovulated immature rats examined the day after mating (4 treated, 5 controls).
results.detail: The study did not directly measure PDE3 binding or activity in the oocytes from the fertilization experiment.
results.quote:
On day 1
after mating, none of the ovulated oocytes in immature rats re-
ceiving Org 9935 showed signs of fertilization (Table II).

results.finding: PHEXXI finished-product extracts (3 rabbits per extraction vehicle) produced daily vaginal irritation scores of 0 to 2, the same range as controls.
results.detail: The five-day extract study was submitted for the later marketing review. FDA cited earlier local toxicology, low expected systemic absorption, and published ingredient toxicology when agreeing that additional nonclinical studies were unnecessary.
results.quote:
Both control and test article animals had daily vaginal scores of 0 to 2 with more 
frequent erythema score of 2 in the test group compared to the normal saline control group.

results.finding: Oral centchroman advanced to Phase I in 1972 after regulatory review of preclinical data. Animal sample sizes were unreported.
results.detail: Table 1 places some longer-term toxicology studies during later dose-ranging work. The initial Phase I decision followed the earlier regulatory animal toxicity studies.
results.quote:
It may 
be mentioned that at each step beginning with the 
preclinical development along with protocol for the 
next study was submitted to the Drugs Controller 
General of India and after his approval the next study 
was initiated.

results.finding: SILCS diaphragm with nonoxynol-9 gel averaged 0 progressively motile sperm per high-power field in a crossover study with 14 couples completing at least one test cycle.
results.detail: The 14 couples are the evaluable crossover sample. The excerpt gives no sample size specific to the nonoxynol-9 arm.
results.quote: The SILCS metal spring diaphragms used with N-9 gel reduced the average number of progressively motile sperm per high power field in the cervical mucus from a baseline of 12.5 to 0, while use of this device with lubricant reduced the number to 0.5.

results.finding: Women&More received ethics approval to start its weekly oral mifepristone contraceptive study and enrolled more than 400 participants by year-end 2025.
results.detail: The source describes a goal of registering mifepristone for contraception if results are positive. It does not establish that Women&More is a pivotal study.
results.quote:
On
March 31, 2025
, Leiden University Medical Center officially rece
ived Medical Ethics Committee approval to start the Women&More study.

case_label = "Approach". Reason: The development programme distinguishes two approaches whose early efficacy tests measure different biological effects.

title = "Self-administered nonhormonal contraception with first-year typical-use pregnancy risk below 1%". Reason: The current title also describes products already available and omits the effectiveness target that distinguishes the breakthrough.

definition = "A reversible, hormone-free contraceptive that a woman administers herself without placing a device in the uterus. Fewer than 1% of users experience an unintended pregnancy during the first year of typical use, which includes inconsistent or incorrect use. Vaginal products are within scope. An existing nonhormonal vaginal gel, Phexxi, had a cumulative pregnancy probability of 13.7% over seven cycles in its pivotal trial.". Reason: The current definition says the contraceptive causes pregnancies and gives readers no comparison with an existing self-administered product.

goal.need = "In surveys across 52 countries in 2005\u20132014, 26% of married women who wanted to avoid pregnancy and used no contraception cited side effects or health risks. In one year, about 17 in 100 diaphragm users and 21 in 100 internal-condom users become pregnant. A copper IUD offers greater protection but requires a clinician to place it in the uterus. Comparable protection from a method women use themselves would give those who wish to avoid both hormones and insertion another choice. Tolerability still matters: even a hormone-free vaginal gel can cause burning or itching.". Reason: The current rationale gives failure rates but leaves out who faces the choice and why tolerability still matters with a hormone-free product.

add statement by Science for Africa Foundation, Grand Challenges Africa, Strengthening the Contraceptive Research and Development Ecosystem in Africa, 2022: "self-administered by women (preferred over provider administered methods)". Reason: The 2022 call explicitly identifies self-administration and excludes intrauterine approaches, two features missing from the existing programme statements.

add statement by Review Panel, Assessment of the Contraceptive Research Activities of the Eunice Kennedy Shriver National Institute of Child Health and Human Development, 2015: "The Panel recommends additional development of female contraceptive modalities that are delivered to the reproductive tract". Reason: The review panel documented why it supported direct reproductive-tract delivery while taking a more cautious view of ovarian targets.
add case "Intravaginal". Reason: Intravaginal products account for the postcoital evidence currently recorded without a case.
add case "Systemic". Reason: The programme also solicited systemic methods, for which a vaginal product’s postcoital result cannot establish efficacy.

add milestone after None: "A contraceptive candidate shows activity through its proposed mechanism in a screening model.". Reason: The existing sequence starts with readiness for human testing and omits the earlier laboratory demonstration of contraceptive activity.
